AnswerOut.description: What a question came to: how it ended, every query tried, and the table, chart and explanation when it ran.
AnswerOut.title: AnswerOut

AskIn.description: A visitor's question, in their own words. Nothing else is accepted next to it.
AskIn.title: AskIn

AttemptOut.description:
One query the model wrote, and the layer and rule that stopped it, or none when it ran.

`sql` is the model's own text: untrusted, to be shown as text and never run or rendered as markup.
AttemptOut.title: AttemptOut

BoxOut.description:
Where a field is printed: its page (from 1), the four corners of the words, and how sure the service is.

Corners are `x, y` as a share of the page's width and height, clockwise from the top left. `confidence` is the
words' own certainty times how well they match the value, and `band` is that number in a word, so the board
never says it with colour alone.
BoxOut.title: BoxOut

ChartOut.description: A chart, as a Vega-Lite 5 spec built by this service from the result (never by the model).
ChartOut.title: ChartOut

CheckId.description: The name of each check: what the API reports, what the board's words are keyed by, what a repair names.
CheckId.title: CheckId

CheckOut.description: One check's verdict, with the numbers that disagree and the fields it is about.
CheckOut.title: CheckOut

ColumnDescriptionOut.description: A column of the semantic layer, as the model is told of it.
ColumnDescriptionOut.title: ColumnDescriptionOut

ColumnOut.description: One column of a result: its name and the kind of value it holds.
ColumnOut.title: ColumnOut

CorrectionIn.description:
A correction: which field, and the text the visitor typed into it. Empty text empties the field.

The field's path is in the body and not in the address: a path such as `line_items.0.total` has dots in it, and
the site's server only forwards addresses whose parts are plain identifiers.
CorrectionIn.title: CorrectionIn

CorrectionOut.description: One correction a visitor made: which field, what it was and what it became.
CorrectionOut.title: CorrectionOut

DimensionOut.description: A way to slice a metric, with its exact definition.
DimensionOut.title: DimensionOut

DocumentListOut.description: The visitor's documents of the hour, newest first.
DocumentListOut.title: DocumentListOut

DocumentOut.description: A document as the API shows it: where it is, and once it is read, everything that was made of it.
DocumentOut.title: DocumentOut

DocumentState.description: Where a document is in the pipeline.
DocumentState.title: DocumentState

DocumentSummaryOut.description: A document in a list: enough to find it again and see how it stands.
DocumentSummaryOut.title: DocumentSummaryOut

DuplicateOut.description: The document this one repeats: one of the visitor's own, or one of the samples, with the same content or not.
DuplicateOut.title: DuplicateOut

ErrorDetail.description:
What went wrong, as a stable code and a sentence for people.

`fields` names the fields a 422 faults, and `resets_at` says when a daily limit starts again.
ErrorDetail.title: ErrorDetail

ErrorOut.description: The error shape the whole platform answers with, as the OpenAPI document describes it.
ErrorOut.title: ErrorOut

FailureCode.description: Why a document has no result.
FailureCode.title: FailureCode

FailureOut.description: Why a document has no result: the code the board has words for, and a sentence for someone reading the API.
FailureOut.title: FailureOut

FieldOut.description: One field of the invoice: its value as text, its box when it was found on the page, and what the checks say.
FieldOut.title: FieldOut

JoinOut.description: An allowed join: two columns that may be set equal.
JoinOut.title: JoinOut

JournalLineOut.description: One line of a journal entry: an account, and an amount on one side.
JournalLineOut.title: JournalLineOut

JournalOut.description: A balanced journal entry as the board shows it: amounts as decimal strings, with the two totals.
JournalOut.title: JournalOut

Layer.description: The defences a query passes through, in order. Each can stop it.
Layer.title: Layer

LimitsOut.description: The limits LB-03 enforces, which are the ones its datasheet promises.
LimitsOut.title: LimitsOut

MetricOut.description: A metric: what it means, and the exact definition a question that names it is given.
MetricOut.title: MetricOut

QuotaOut.description: A visitor's documents today, the limits, and whether the service can read documents at all right now.
QuotaOut.title: QuotaOut

RangeOut.description: A date phrase the resolver understands, and the dates it means counted from the data's last day.
RangeOut.title: RangeOut

ReadinessOut.description: The readiness answer: for each system, whether it can serve right now.
ReadinessOut.title: ReadinessOut

ResultOut.description: The table a query returned, and the checked SQL that produced it.
ResultOut.title: ResultOut

Rule.description: What a layer found wrong. Each rule belongs to one layer and is either worth a second try or not.
Rule.title: Rule

SemanticLayerOut.description: The semantic layer: everything the model is told about the data, and so everything a query may use.
SemanticLayerOut.title: SemanticLayerOut

Severity.description: Whether a failed check stops the export (an error) or only asks for a look (a warning).
Severity.title: Severity

StepOut.description: One step of a document's run: what it was, how it ended, how long it took, and a few counts about it.
StepOut.title: StepOut

TableOut.description: A table of the semantic layer.
TableOut.title: TableOut

UploadIn.description: The upload: exactly one part, `file`. Nothing else is accepted next to it.
UploadIn.title: UploadIn

info.description: The API behind the LB systems built on Flask.
info.title: LB Flask systems

get.summary: Report that the process is up. It checks nothing else, so a database blip never restarts it.
List the visitor's documents of the hour, newest first, so the board can find them after a reload.

post.description:
Answers 202 at once with the document in state `uploaded`; poll it to watch it being read. Counts against
the visitor's 10 documents a day, which the service enforces itself, and two documents are read at a time.
A document the service itself fails to read is not counted, for up to three such documents a day.
post.summary: Upload an invoice, a credit note or a till receipt (PDF, PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 10 MB and 5 pages).

delete.summary: Delete a document that has ended, with its files. A document still being read can't be deleted yet.

get.summary: Read one document: its state while it is being read, and when it is ready its fields, boxes and checks.

post.description:
A corrected field counts as confirmed by the visitor and loses its box. The duplicate check and the journal
entry are made again from the corrected reading. Answers 200 with the whole document as it now stands.
post.summary: Correct one field of a read document: every check runs again, and the correction is recorded.

get.description: The CSV exports are refused (409) while a failed check stops the export. The JSON always goes.

200.description: The export: a CSV file (UTF-8 with a byte order mark) or the JSON of the whole reading.

get.summary: Export a read document: its lines or its journal entry as CSV, or everything as JSON.

200.description: The JPEG picture of one page.

get.summary: Read the picture of one page of the visitor's document, for the viewer. Never served any other way.
Read how many documents the visitor has left today, how many are being read, and the limits.

post.description:
Counts against the visitor's 25 questions a day, which the service enforces itself, and a
visitor has one question running at a time. A question the service itself fails to answer is not
counted, for up to five such questions a day: after that a failed question counts too.
post.summary: Answer a question about the sales data, synchronously: the SQL, the table, a chart and an explanation.

get.summary: Read how many questions the visitor has left today, and the limits LB-05 enforces.
Read the semantic layer: the tables, joins, metrics and slices a question may use, and what each means.
Report whether every system can serve, for the container's readiness check.
